solution:
Option C, tropical deciduous forests.

The chapter's one worked example of gathering is a monsoon, that is tropical deciduous, forest: kath is collected from monsoon forests from Khair trees. It also says the occupation is carried out in all the forest covered regions of the world, so the question is which of them carries it MAINLY.

Option D is the trap, and the chapter rules it out explicitly. The equatorial forests are dense and evergreen, the climate is humid and unhealthy, and due to the disturbance of reptiles and insects collection of forest products is NOT done on a large scale there.

Options A and B name temperate forests. The products the chapter lists for gathering - fruits, roots and tubers, leaves, flowers, medicinal plants, gum, lac, honey, wax and rubber - are tropical forest products, and lac, kath and rubber in particular come from monsoon and tropical forests rather than temperate ones.

Option B: shallow seas, confluence of warm and cold ocean currents, growth of planktons, cold climate.

The chapter names two physical factors first and separately, before all the others. The first is a wide expanse of the continental shelf with the presence of shallow water. The second is the confluence of warm and cold currents and the subsequent growth of abundant plankton, AS A RESULT OF WHICH fishing grounds or banks develop. Option B is the only one of the four that contains that second factor, and it is the factor the chapter credits with creating a fishing ground in the first place. Its example is the warm Kuroshio current meeting the cold Oyashio current, which favours the coastal area near Japan.

Option A is wrong on its face: it says hot climate, whereas the chapter says a cold climate in the temperate regions facilitates preservation of fish and that tropical countries must develop artificial refrigeration instead.

Options C and D are harder, because every element in them is something the chapter does name - continental shelf, plankton, cold climate, good fishing skills, broken coasts. But each replaces the current-confluence with a secondary factor: C with traditional skills, which the chapter lists as a human factor, and D with a broken coast line, which it credits with providing port facilities rather than fish. Neither describes what makes a LOCATION ideal as precisely as B.

Option C, mining. The chapter states it in those words: this activity depends solely on the presence of minerals and not related to latitude directly.

The reason is that minerals were placed by geology rather than by climate, and the chapter adds that their distribution is highly uneven in the world. The map bears it out - mining stars appear on every continent except Antarctica, from the far north to the southern tips, in no latitudinal band at all.

Each of the other three does follow latitude. Lumbering is mostly practised in the coniferous regions, which lie in a high-latitude belt. Fishing follows the continental shelves and the meetings of warm and cold currents. Agriculture thins towards the poles and is limited by climate, which the chapter names as the first of its major physical factors.

Option B: monoculture, use of machinery, tropical, cereal production.

Three of its four elements come straight from the chapter's own description of extensive commercial agriculture: it is monocultural; it is capital intensive with more use of modern machinery, used from sowing to harvesting; and wheat and maize are the major crops, that is cereal production.

No other option carries the machinery. A says use of water instead, D says scientific know how and production of pulses, and C says manual labour, equator, Thailand and horticulture, which describes a different kind of farming altogether.

[Textbook imprecision: option B calls the region TROPICAL, and the chapter places extensive commercial agriculture on the TEMPERATE grasslands - Steppes, Praries, Downs, Pampas and Velds. So the intended answer is imperfect on its fourth element. It remains the best of the four, because the alternatives are wrong on the crop, the labour or the machinery, which are the defining features; the correct region to give in a written answer is temperate grassland, not tropical.]
